To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the vesicular glutamatergic neurons are present in the rat trigeminally ganglion, and that these neurons express transient receptor potential ankeyrin 1 (TrpA1), a cold and mechanical nociceptor.

the majority of VGLUT+ TRPA1+ trigeminal ganglionic neurons are non-peptideric, that VGLUT1 is present in myelinated afferent neurons and VGLUT 2 in non-myelinated afferents, and that VGLUT 1 is not upregulated following inflammation.
the fraction of Vglut2-expressing, TRPA1-positive neurons increases after inflammation, suggesting a potential role of Vglut1 in TRPA1-induced pain hypersensitivity.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the expression of VGlut1/2 and their co-expression with TRPA1 in the trigeminal ganglia of rats.
the expression of the vesicular glutamatergic system (VGLUT) in the TRPA+ neurons in the rat vibrissal pad, and its change following inflammation.
the role of glutamate in TRPA1-induced nociception.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
VGLUT1 is involved in the glutamatergic signaling in TRPA-positive neurons in the rat, and that VGLUT 2 is involved in the same in the mouse.
VGLUT1 is expressed in a small fraction of the TRPA+ neurons and VGLUT 2 is expressed in a majority of TRPA+ neurons.

VGLUT1 is expressed by a small population of myelinated TRPA1+ sensory neurons, whereas VGLUT2 is expressed by the majority of peptideric, non-peptideric, myelinated and unmyelinated TRPA+ sensory neurons.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the VGLUT1- and VGLUT 2-expressing neurons are differentially involved in the glutamatergic signaling in TRPA 1+ neurons, and the TRPA 1-mediated glutamate signaling in the VGLUT 1+ neurons is not affected by the inflammation, whereas that in the VGLVT 2+ neurons is enhanced by inflammation.
the TRPA1-expressing neurons in the trigeminal ganglia express VGLUTs, which may play a role, at least in part, in the glutamatergic signaling in these neurons.
VGLUT1 is involved in the mechanotransduction in the myelinated afferent neurons, and VGLUT 2 is involved in the nociception in the peptiderg neurons.
The main takeaway from our work is that
VGLUT1- and VGLUT-2-expressing neurons co-express TRPA1 in the rat trigeminus ganglion.
TRPA1+ sensory neurons express both VGLUT2 and VGLUT3, and that the fraction and the expression level of VGLUT3+ TRPA1+ cells increases significantly following inflammation.
both VGLVTs are involved in the VGLUT-mediated glutamate signaling in the TRPA+ neurons, and that VGLUT1 is expressed in a small fraction of the TRPV1+ neurons.
